A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same authors' IB-based color-naming and IICLL research. The text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v2 has no appendices; v3 includes Appendices A-M.

before.justification: v2 reports original English color-naming measurements in Table 1 and simulated IICLL outcomes in Figure 1.

after.justification: v3 reports original multi-model naming experiments, IICLL simulations, Shepard-circle results and additional empirical analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same core IICLL procedure: learn sampled stimulus-pseudoword pairs in context, label the full stimulus space and transmit sampled outputs to subsequent generations. v3 documents constrained decoding and conversation history, but does not establish that these revise v2's underlying procedure. Shepard circles use the existing paradigm.

E1.justification: v3 adds an actually evaluated semantic domain: 64 Shepard-circle stimuli varying in radius and spoke angle, categorized through Gemini IICLL (Section 4.3, Figure 5). This substantially extends the color-only coverage of v2. The WCS, English naming and human color-learning reference datasets remain.

E2.justification: English naming comparisons expand beyond Gemini and Llama to include Gemma, Qwen, OLMo and GPT-2; the main IICLL comparison adds Gemma and Qwen. Appendix M also evaluates a new nearest-neighbor sRGB classifier, NN-rgb, against the four main LLMs for k=14. Human and IB reference comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v3 systematically evaluates model-size and base/instruction-tuned variants, OLMo training checkpoints, CIELAB inputs and history-window settings of 0, 10, 20 and 50. These introduce substantial additional evaluation designs. Color IICLL is restricted to sRGB features, whereas v2 also reports Gemini image-input chains. Newly specified defaults for retained experiments are documentation rather than established setting changes.

E4.justification: v3 adds CIELAB sensitivity tests, OLMo training-trajectory analysis, history-window ablations, smaller-model failure analysis and a nearest-neighbor test of the clustering explanation (Appendices C, F, K-M). Its explicit rotation analysis develops the hypothetical-variant check briefly mentioned in v2. Conversely, v2's reported robustness to imperceptible input noise is omitted.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 reports English naming means and standard deviations across ten random seeds; v3 does not retain equivalent seed/SD reporting for its naming plots. Both versions show 95% confidence intervals for IICLL. v3 additionally specifies a normal-distribution assumption for rotation-analysis intervals, without establishing an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: The result set expands substantially beyond v2's two-model study. New outcomes include single-category collapse in 19 of 20 smaller-model chains (Appendix L), Gemini outperforming NN-rgb on all three reported k=14 metrics (Appendix M), and increasingly structured Shepard-circle categories (Figure 5). v2's Gemini image-input color-IICLL results are no longer presented. These are added or removed findings, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 adds Bayesian iterated-learning convergence conditions and the stationary-prior result in Section 2.3. Appendix A explicitly specifies the meaning prior, Bayesian listener and accuracy/KL-distortion relationship, beyond v2's shorter mathematical account. The central IB objective remains unchanged, and no new original theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central efficiency-bias claim remains, but v3 adds major claims about widespread English-naming failures and systematic associations with size and instruction tuning. Its abstract emphasizes that only Gemini among tested models spans the human complexity range. The introduction and discussion also add tentative applicability beyond color, supported by Shepard circles, expanding v2's contribution scope.

C2.justification: Beyond v2's brief size/modality speculation, v3 interprets low English alignment as potentially compatible with other human color systems, discusses in-context capacity and collapse, and tests a simple clustering explanation. It explicitly acknowledges uncertainty about the bias's origins, the absence of communication pressure and limited cross-domain evidence. These substantially develop mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 supplies model IDs, example prompts, allowed labels, decoding details, 6k-example training sets, the ten-interaction history window, generation limits and stopping rules. Its reproducibility statement identifies source code/data access and promises experiment-code release upon publication. These greatly expand v2's sparse implementation disclosures without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1-2.3 substantially expand positioning against previous LLM color studies, neural iterated learning and emergent communication. Added discussions include Abdou et al., Patel and Pavlick, Marjieh et al., Ren et al. and Carlsson et al. The unresolved I-ICL citation in v2 is replaced by an explicit relationship to Zhu and Griffiths (2024).

P1.justification: v3 changes the title and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction and explanatory narrative. Background becomes separate motivation, IB and iterated-learning subsections; experimental setup and results are separated; the short conclusion becomes an extended discussion. Organized technical appendices and a reproducibility statement substantially restructure the document.

P2.justification: v2's composite Figure 1 is reorganized and redrawn across separate overview, naming, trajectory and time-course displays in v3 Figures 1-4. v3 adds numerous domain and appendix figures, including model-specific panels and category maps. The numerical results table is removed, while a model-inventory table is introduced, substantially changing visual organization.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidential support and reproducibility of v2's two-model study. Broader comparisons reveal failure boundaries, while history-window tests and the NN-rgb baseline directly examine alternative explanations for category formation. Detailed procedures and clearer limitations make the conclusions easier to assess. These gains outweigh the loss of explicit English-naming seed/SD reporting and image-input color-IICLL results. The Shepard-circle extension remains preliminary, and experiment code is still only promised.
